Seminar Title:

Influence of hot-rolling temperature on grain boundary evolution and tensile behaviour of a fully austenitic medium-Mn steel

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Metallurgical and Materials Engineering

Speaker Name:

Anant Kumar ( Rollno : 524mm1005)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Metallurgical and Materials Engineering Department

Date and Time:

30 Sep 2026 4:30 PM

Contact:

Arnab Sarkar

Abstract:

The development of lightweight steels with an excellent combination of strength and ductility, and reduced processing steps, is important for advanced structural and automotive applications. In this study, a fully austenitic medium-manganese steel alloyed with Mn, Al, Cr, Ni, and C was developed, and the effects of processing temperature on its microstructure, grain-boundary characteristics, phase stability, and tensile properties were systematically investigated. The steel was produced using an open-air induction furnace via melting and casting routes, followed by homogenization, hot forging, reheating, and continuous hot rolling. Reheating was conducted at 1173K, 1273K, and 1373 K for 105 minutes, followed by hot rolling at 1120K, 1210K, and 1300 K. Thermodynamic phase-equilibrium calculations were used to optimize the processing conditions and suppress cementite formation, enabling retention of a fully austenitic structure. XRD, SEM, and EBSD analyses confirmed the stability of the single-phase austenitic matrix after hot rolling and tensile deformation. The rolling temperature strongly affected grain morphology, refinement, crystallographic texture, grain-orientation spread, and grain-boundary character distribution. Variations in LAGBs, HAGBs, and CSL boundaries indicated changes in deformation and recovery behavior. Higher rolling temperatures promoted the formation of special CSL boundaries and favourable HAGB distributions, improving grain-boundary stability. The steel exhibited a favourable strength&ndashductility combination, attributed to stable austenite and dislocation-mediated deformation. Fractography images revealed predominantly ductile fracture with microvoid dimples and tearing ridges. Overall, controlling hot-rolling temperature offers an effective route to tailor grain-boundary characteristics and optimize the mechanical performance of lightweight medium-manganese steels.
